##The plan

We can find the area of each trapezoid by multiplying its width by the average of the values of $f(x)$ at the left and right endpoints.

![A trapezoid whose bases are vertical has width b minus a. The left, shorter base has height f of a. The right, taller base has height f of b.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e2a5fa8a5479bf6d93a5f89670f35578f1dc0fad) 

$\text{area of trapezoid}=(b-a)\left( \dfrac{f(a)+f(b)}{2} \right)$

Then we *sum* all of the areas.

## Area of the trapezoids

Let's find the area of the first trapezoid:

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_1 &= (0-(-1)) \cdot \dfrac{f(-1)+f(0)}{2} \\\\
&= 1\cdot \dfrac{18}{2} \\\\
&=9
\end{align}$

We can repeat the process for the remaining trapezoids.

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_2 &= (1-0) \cdot \dfrac{f(0)+f(1)}{2} \\\\
&= 1\cdot  \dfrac{13}{2} \\\\
&=6.5
\end{align}$

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_3 &= (2-1) \cdot \dfrac{f(1)+f(2)}{2} \\\\
&= 1\cdot \dfrac{10}{2} \\\\
&=5
\end{align}$

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_4 &= (3-2) \cdot \dfrac{f(2)+f(3)}{2} \\\\
&= 1\cdot  \dfrac{9}{2} \\\\
&=4.5
\end{align}$

question.content:
**Approximate the area between the $x$-axis and $f(x)$ from $x = -1$ to $x = 3$ using a *trapezoidal sum* with $4$ equal subdivisions.**

 | |  ||||
:-: | -: | -: | -: | -:
$x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ 
$f(x)$ | $7$ | $11$ | $2$ | $8$ | $1$

The approximate area is [[☃ numeric-input 1]]
